messages:
Alex: Hey, folks — running into a flaky streaming issue on Vercel Edge. ReadableStream starts, a few chunks then hang forever. Sometimes we see a 401 mid-stream and the client never recovers. Billing shows duplicate tokens for some requests. Anyone seen this?

Maya: Repro steps I used:
```
// Next.js edge route
export default async function handler(req) {
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_KEY}` },
    body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'rw-medium', stream: true, prompt: 'hello' })
  })
  const reader = res.body.getReader()
  while (true) {
    const { done, value } = await reader.read()
    if (done) break
    // process chunk
  }
}
```
We get one or two chunks then reader.read() never resolves. Network panel shows an open SSE-ish connection. Sometimes log shows `401 invalid token` around the same time.

Jamie (Support): Thanks — can you paste the SDK version and exact token expiry time (if available)? Also any proxy or gateway in front? :thinking:

Maya: Using `@redwood/inference-js@0.8.1` from unpkg in the edge bundle. Token is long-lived (service key) — logs show `token expired` at "2026-02-02T03:12:18Z" but the request was at 03:12:30Z so not sure how expiry aligns. No external proxy.

Rita (Eng): This sounds like two possible things:
1) Edge runtime + SDK mismatch where the fetch body is converted differently (ReadableStream vs Node stream).
2) Retry-on-error behavior causing duplicate billing when the server replays partial chunks after a reconnect.

Sam (DevEx): Quick check: older SDK builds bundled a Node stream polyfill that caused `Content-Length`/Transfer-Encoding interplay on Vercel edge and could result in the connection left open. Can you confirm if your build includes `stream-polyfill` or if you're bundling Node core shims?

Maya: We're using webpack/next default; didn't explicitly include shims. I can inspect the bundle.

Maya: Also attaching a tiny request/response excerpt from our logs (sanitized):
```
-> POST /v1/generate 200 (stream)
<- chunk: "data: {\"token\":\"..\"}\n\n"
<- chunk: "data: {\"text\":\"hi\"}\n\n"
<- error: "401 token expired"
<- connection: keep-alive (still open)
```

Jamie (Support): Can you try two quick experiments?
- pin the SDK to the edge build: `@redwood/inference-js@1.2.0-edge`
- send header `x-redwood-no-retry: 1` to disable server automatic reconnects and see if the hang still happens.

Maya: Trying now...

Deploy Bot: Deploy started: next-landing @ vercel — build id 03a7f

Maya: With `1.2.0-edge` + `x-redwood-no-retry` the stream now closes cleanly after chunks. No 401 midstream in this run. :relieved:

Rita (Eng): Great — that indicates the issue is in the older SDK behavior that attempted client-side/edge retries and left the readable stream unresolved when a server-side auth error happened. We'll track as a bug. Short-term workaround: use edge build or set `x-redwood-no-retry`.

Sam (DevEx): Follow-up: if you must stay on 0.8.x for some reason, set `fetch` option `keepalive: false` and attach an AbortSignal that times out at 30-60s so reader doesn't hang forever.

Maya: Noted. One more thing: we saw duplicate charge for the request that had a retry. Is that expected?

Jamie (Support): Unfortunately yes — if a client retries after partial output (and server accepted the initial request) the platform may record token usage for both attempts. That's why we added the `x-redwood-no-retry` header and improved the edge build behavior to avoid automatic retries during streams.

Kyle (Product): Filing a ticket to mark this as a P1 if it affects billed traffic on Dedicated customers. Also tracking a release to backport the edge build fix into the next 0.8.x patch.

Rita (Eng): Action items for eng:
- Create a small failing test reproducing ReadableStream hang in Vercel Edge (done locally).
- Patch SDK to avoid polyfill-driven retry in edge bundles.
- Add server-side guard to return 4xx immediately (no attempted replay) when auth fails mid-stream.

Maya: Thanks everyone — workaround works. Will upgrade to 1.2.0-edge and report back if anything else shows up. :thumbsup:

Jamie (Support): If you can share a short bundle map showing `stream-polyfill` presence, we can prioritize the backport. Otherwise we'll push a patch and announce in #support and #eng-runtime.

Maya: I'll attach bundle map once it's available. Appreciate the quick help!
